scope.candidate_path: ordinary Leopard2 benchmark entry paths; no prevalidated binding executable was timed

ratio_orientation: Leopard1 time divided by Leopard2 time; values above one favor Leopard2

metric_semantics.encode: Leopard1 encode execution divided by ordinary Leopard2 encode execution
metric_semantics.decode_first: Leopard1 decode including setup divided by Leopard2 decode execution plus one full decode-plan setup
metric_semantics.decode_reuse: Leopard1 decode including setup divided by Leopard2 decode execution plus decode-plan setup amortized over 87381 executions

campaign.statistics: geometric ratio with Student-t 95 percent interval over three independent ABBA round log contrasts

interpretation.ordinary_tiny_cells: Leopard2 remains slower than exact main at K=3 and K=4 for both sizes. It also remains slower at K=8 except that reused decode at 256 bytes is approximately at parity but still below one in every measured position.
interpretation.structural_crossover: Ordinary Leopard2 encode and heavily reused decode are faster in every measured K=24 and K=32 cell.
interpretation.first_decode: Decode with a fresh plan remains slower than exact main in every measured cell because Leopard2 plan setup dominates these tiny workloads.
interpretation.residual_attribution: The R=1 arithmetic is no longer the tiny-cell bottleneck. Prior same-binary TSC attribution at 07391da measured K3/B64 raw fixed encode at 7.4 cycles, a prevalidated binding at 38.8 cycles, and the ordinary public encode at 51.9 cycles; decode measured 8.2, 32.7, and 52.9 cycles respectively. The residual is pointer-range, null, overlap, alias, error-order, immutable-object, and plan/setup validation that exact main does not provide at the same contract strength.
interpretation.exhausted_safe_scope: The campaign implementation includes fixed register-resident B64/B256 AVX2 reducers, setup-qualified immutable bindings, and packed ordinary encode, batch, reusable-plan, and one-shot decode terminals. Removing the remaining K3/K4 public-call checks would weaken documented Leopard2 safety semantics; callers that can establish those invariants ahead of time use the separate prevalidated binding path. This is a bounded API-semantics exception, not evidence against the redundancy-side algorithm.
interpretation.binding_directional_control: A separate non-authoritative same-binary K3/B64 screen measured the fixed prevalidated binding at 0.002719 microseconds encode and 0.002656 microseconds decode versus 0.011676 and 0.009467 for the mature binding. It is excluded from the exact-main ratios above because it is a different API contract.
interpretation.claim_limit: This campaign establishes the sampled R=1 regions only; it does not claim that ordinary Leopard2 wins all tiny K values or all shard sizes.
